title: Give Your Chat Agent a Voice — Luke Harries, Head of Growth, ElevenLabs
talk_summary: A product pitch from ElevenLabs for a 'voice engine' wrapper that adds speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and turn-taking around an existing chat agent via a server SDK, plus a client SDK widget and UI components. The only generalizable idea is packaging a capability as a thin wrapper/proxy around an existing agent rather than rebuilding it, and shipping a 'skill' so a coding agent can do the integration in one prompt.

takeaways.technique: Thin wrapper/proxy around existing agent instead of rebuild
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose a new capability as a first-class primitive that attaches to an existing agent: each new session starts a loop that proxies requests to the already-built chat agent, so existing tool calling, RAG, and evals are reused untouched.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will kick off this loop and just kind of proxy all the stuff to your to your existing chat agent

takeaways.technique: Ship an integration 'skill' the coding agent can execute in one prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: The release bundles a skill containing best-practice integration steps; a coding agent analyzes the codebase, finds the chat agent, and writes the wrapper code itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will come with a skill which basically has all the best in class stuff. And then it's literally one prompt
